title: Rescue of the Lost Battalion
photoNote: Soldiers of the 442nd Regimental Combat Team hiking up a muddy road in France, late 1944. U.S. Army Signal Corps, public domain. From the weeks after the rescue, not the day itself.
body:
To reach 211 trapped Texans, a unit of Japanese American soldiers paid with hundreds of casualties of its own.

30 October 1944. In the cold, wet forests of the Vosges Mountains in eastern France, the 1st Battalion of the 141st Infantry had been cut off by German troops since 24 October. About 275 men were surrounded.

The 442nd Regimental Combat Team was sent to get them out. It was a segregated unit of Nisei, the American born sons of Japanese immigrants, and it had been pulled out of a rest after liberating the towns of Bruyères and Biffontaine. For days its men attacked uphill through German positions in the trees.

On 30 October they broke through. 211 men of the Lost Battalion walked out.

By most counts the 442nd took more casualties in the rescue than the number of men it saved. In 1962 Texas made its veterans honorary Texans.

video.note: AMERICAN-JAPANESE TROOPS, MEURTHE MOSELLE, FRANCE, 30 and 31 October 1944. U.S. Army Signal Corps film 111-ADC-3423 (NARA 17226), silent. Shot card: Japanese American infantrymen advance through the woods of the Vosges, and 'soldiers of the 1st Bn in a group walk toward the camera in the woods. The men look tired; some have several days growth of beard.' Clip: Nisei soldiers climb a forest trail, a Nisei soldier on a field phone, then the men of the 1st Battalion walking out. U.S. government work, public domain (NARA's blanket 'possibly copyright' flag on Signal Corps reels). Clip uses 4:59.0 to 5:02.8, 5:24.0 to 5:26.8, and 7:34.0 to 7:43.0.
video.hook: Cut off since 24 October. Here they walk out.
